note: The finish a made place's grounds, paths and water are drawn with over the colours its style pack gives them. Every value is presentation: no recorded position, ground, water, contact, path or pick is changed by it, and a page that reads none of it draws every surface in its pack's flat colour. Each value is a chosen default with its reason, set by eye against the Canopy garden at three fixed views and measured there; not a measured physical property or a safety bound. A later version is another file beside this one.

entries.reason: How far a ground's tone wanders above and below its pack colour across the ground, as a share of that colour. One flat tone to the horizon reads as a painted floor; real grass and paving vary by a tenth or so in brightness over a few metres. Kept small so the pack's colour stays the colour a person chose.
The size of the broad wander in a ground's tone: patches about a house wide, which a person standing sees as uneven ground rather than as a texture.

The size of the finer wander laid over the broad one, about a stride or two, so near ground is not smooth either. Not smaller than this: finer than a metre it flickers at the distances a site is watched from.

How far a ground leans warmer in some patches and cooler in others, as a share of each colour channel: drier and lusher ground differ in hue as well as brightness. Small, so no ground changes its colour name.

How far from a water's edge the ground beside it is drawn wet and darker, fading to dry. Ground at a pond's edge is darker for about an arm's length to a couple of metres; this keeps the water from sitting on the ground like a sheet of colour.
How much darker ground is at the water's very edge, as a share of its colour. Wet soil and stone are about a third darker than dry.
How far in from its edge water reaches its deepest colour. A pond is shallow at its rim and darker towards its middle; a few metres reads as a garden pond, not a lake.
How much lighter water is drawn at its very edge than its pack colour, where the bed shows through shallow water.
How much darker water is drawn at its deepest than its pack colour.

How far light drifting over water brightens and darkens it, as a share of its colour. Moving water must read as moving at a glance from standing height; more than about a tenth reads as a pattern rather than as light on water.
The size of the drifting light on water: a little under two metres, small beside a pond and large enough not to shimmer at a distance.
How fast the light drifts over water: an easy breeze over a still pond, slow enough to read as calm.

How much brighter water is drawn seen at a low angle than looking down into it, as water reflects more of the sky the lower it is seen. Applied as a brightening of the water's own colour, so it works in every shading model a pack may choose.

How much of the real reflection of the world in level water is added to its light; 0 makes no reflection camera at all. Off in this version, by measurement: on the Canopy garden at three fixed views (headless Chrome, Metal, 1280x860, 14 October 2026) the reflection camera took the draws of a frame from 495, 738 and 697 to 907, 1,339 and 1,217, past the finish's budget of no more draws than before. It stays available, at a strength a later version states, once a world's draws leave room for it.

The size, square, of the texture the reflection is drawn into when one is drawn: a pond is a small part of a view and its reflection is broken by the water's light, so a quarter of a full view's width is enough.
